subject.title: fix: forward response-frame meta to clients

question: Should OpenClaw accept optional top-level `res.meta` on the existing v4 Gateway response envelope after this PR is rebased, or require a versioned or alternate metadata contract?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and proven, but the public protocol envelope is compatibility-sensitive because older strict validators generated from the previous schema may reject the additive field.

options.title: Accept additive v4 metadata after rebase
options.body: Resolve conflicts on current main, keep `meta` optional and absent when unused, and treat strict-client tolerance as the v4 compatibility expectation.

options.title: Require versioned metadata
options.body: Pause the PR until maintainers choose a protocol version bump or negotiated capability path for response metadata.

options.title: Use a handler-specific workaround
options.body: Avoid changing the envelope and instead expose dedupe/run metadata inside affected method payloads, accepting a less general contract.

recommendation.title: Accept additive v4 metadata after rebase
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts on current main, keep `meta` optional and absent when unused, and treat strict-client tolerance as the v4 compatibility expectation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits on the shared Gateway protocol and responder type surfaces where Vincent Koc has both current-line and historical ownership signals.
